lobbyists.name: Adam William Chapdelaine
lobbyists.purpose: All legislative, administrative and regulatory matters pertaining to local government before the legislature and executive branch, including the following: • The general appropriations act and supplemental appropriations acts (House 2, the Governor's proposed fiscal 2027 state budget, and supplemental budgets for fiscal year 2026), and all legislation and regulations affecting local government finance, operations and administration; • State and local tax and revenue matters, including the property tax, state taxes and local-option taxing authority, payments-in-lieu-of taxes, municipal fees and charges and state fees and charges that would benefit local government, the administration of the state Lottery and distribution of Lottery proceeds, and the distribution of surtax revenue funding; • Municipal and education aid programs and funding, including Unrestricted General Government Aid, Chapter 70, charter school financing, special education funding, and school transportation reimbursements; • Funding and administration of capital programs benefiting local government including Chapter 90, water-related funding and bond authorizations, the school building assistance program, and municipal infrastructure needs; • Education matters affecting the operation and financing of municipal, regional and other school districts, including vocational and charter schools; • Personnel and labor matters affecting cities and towns, including Civil Service, other post employment benefits (OPEB), municipal health insurance, unemployment insurance (UI), collective bargaining, training, certification and management of public employees, workplace safety, and the composition of the commonwealth employment relations board; • Human services and public health, including delivery of public health services and matters related to public emergencies; • Energy matters, including solar and other renewable energy matters; • Environmental matters, including the cost-benefit analyses of environmental rules and regulations, environmental permitting and permit approval procedures, sustainable water resource funds, recycling and solid water management, PFAS mitigation and other water and land contamination matters; • Municipal planning, permitting, zoning, housing and other matters related to local and regional land use regulation and economic development; • Public works, including use of public rights-of-way and the municipal purchase of utility poles; • All matters related to the administration of local government, including but not limited to elections and actions by local legislative bodies, municipal control over liquor licenses, municipal authority regarding the cannabis industry, the administration of veteran’s benefits, and the modernization of municipal government operations; In these efforts, this legislative agent will communicate with every member of the Massachusetts House of Representatives and Senate, and all corresponding executive branch officials.

lobbyists.name: Jacqueline Marie Hubbard
lobbyists.purpose: NAMI Massachusetts aims to provide direction and guidance on policy issues affecting mental health in the Commonwealth to Affiliates, state agencies, community stakeholders, advocates, and the general public. Legislation is organized by primary area of focus, but categories do often overlap. The work will include the areas below and others as they arise. Equity and Inclusion in Mental Health Access and Services S.709/H.1135: An Act for supportive care for serious mental illness - Senator Cronin/Representative Decker Requires commercial insurers to cover evidence-based care for first-episode psychosis, including 24/7 multidisciplinary wraparound services and assertive community treatment, ensuring parity in mental health coverage. Mental Health as Integral to Overall Health, Addressing Social Determinants of Health S.708/H.1128: An Act preserving access to treatment for patients with serious mental illness - Senator Cronin/Representative Decker This legislation advances patient equity by eliminating prior authorization, step therapy, and other barriers that delay access to medication for individuals with serious mental illness within health insurance carriers or utilization review organizations. S.283/H.383: An Act expanding licensure opportunity for school counselors - Senator Payano/Representative Hamilton/Representative Vargas Streamlines the path for DESE-credentialed school counselors to become Licensed Mental Health Counselors (LMHC) by recognizing prior coursework, supervision hours, and allowing school counselors to sit for the qualifying exam. This increases the number of LMHCs in schools while maintaining licensing standards. Human Rights and Protection Against Discrimination H.2198: An Act reducing emergency department boarding - Representative Decker Prevents individuals from being involuntarily held for more than 72 hours at facilities not authorized by the Department of Mental Health (DMH). Any psychiatric hold exceeding 48 hours at such facilities must be referred to the Committee on Public Counsel Services for appointment of counsel. S.1389/H.2211: An Act modernizing the 6 fundamental rights - Senator Cyr/Representative Higgins Establishes the statutory rights of all people receiving mental health services in state hospitals, community mental health centers, and residential programs or inpatient facilities. Includes access to a telephone/videophone, ability to send and receive mail, the right to receive or refuse visitors, a humane psychological and physical environment, the ability to see attorneys, doctors, and mental health professionals, and daily access to the outdoors. Person-Centered Mental Health Support for Individuals and Families S.1407: Resolve to ensure delivery of mental health services to adults with acute mental illness - Senator E. Kennedy Creates a special commission to study the staffing levels and delivery of services for case managers at the Department of Mental Health (DMH) tasked with serving adults with acute mental illness. Criminal Justice and the Decriminalization of Mental Health S1386/H3291/H3313 An Act to transfer Bridgewater State Hospital from the Department of Corrections to the Department of Mental Health - Senator Creem/Representative Barber/Representative Decker Will transfer oversight of Bridgewater State Hospital (BSH) to the Department of Mental Health (DMH) from the Department of Corrections (DOC). H.2201: An Act relative to ensuring quality mental health services in state correctional facilities - Representative Decker Allows for the Commissioner of the Department of Mental Health (DMH) to have supervision of mental health services to incarcerated individuals under the custody of the Department of Corrections (DOC).

lobbyists.purpose: Eneida Román, CEO of We Are ALX, will serve as the organization’s designated lobbyist to advocate for policies and budgetary measures that advance Latino prosperity, racial equity, and economic mobility in Massachusetts. Her lobbying activities will focus on increasing equitable access to state-funded economic development programs, small business support, workforce development initiatives, and culturally responsive education and childcare services for Latino communities. Areas of legislative and budgetary interest include, but are not limited to: Economic and workforce development legislation that expands access to capital, grants, and training for Minority- and Women-Owned Business Enterprises (MWBEs), particularly Latino-owned businesses. Education and early childhood policies that support Latino educators, family childcare providers, and dual-language learners. Support for public funding, including line items in the Massachusetts state budget, that align with ALX’s mission to elevate Latino leadership and prosperity. Engagement with Executive Office of Economic Development, Executive Office of Education, and the Governor’s Latino Empowerment Council, among others. ALX’s advocacy includes direct engagement with legislators, committee chairs, and agency officials, including members of the Massachusetts Black and Latino Legislative Caucus. Specific legislation and bill numbers will be added as filed and relevant to our organizational priorities.
